newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares show no sign of giving up gains.
newsitem.headline: German shares show no sign of giving up gains.

text.p: Germany's share market shows no sign of letting up steam on the race to new record highs after reaching fresh records in bourse trade on Thursday.
Dealers have set their sights on the 30-share DAX index reaching 4,500 points in the coming days, even though volumes have been lower than in previous days.
The IBIS DAX was down 1.68 points at 4,456.98 points in late afternoon dealings but above the bourse session when the DAX ended up 17.21 points at 4,438.93 points.
"It's hard to predict when this market is going to stop moving higher," said one Frankfurt dealer.
"We are seeing some rounds of profit-taking but the buyers come right back," the dealer said.
Early gains on Wall Street underpinned the German share market, which has been drawing strength for weeks from the U.S. advance to record levels.
The dollar resuming its upward trend against the mark, which makes German exports more competitive, also helped boost market sentiment.
Daimler-Benz AG stole the spotlight, ending bourse trade down 4.50 marks at 154.80 marks despite first-half sales and operating profit figures generally at market expectations.
Daimler shares had risen nearly 10 percent this week ahead of the results, which were released at a news conference in London, and traders tied the losses to profit-taking.
The Stuttgart-based industrial group said operating profit for the first half rose to 1.849 billion marks from 827 million marks in the year-ago period.
Traders also kept their focus on the banking sector, which has been moving higher on takeover speculation after Vereinsbank and Hypo-Bank said on July 21 that they planned to merge.
Vereinsbank ended the bourse down two marks at 101 marks and Hypo-Bank fell 1.07 marks to 76.53 marks. Insurer Allianz AG, a Hypo-Bank shareholder, fell 9.50 marks to 1,470.
Vereinsbank on Thursday detailed terms of its planned merger with Hypo-Bank, saying its offer to exchange one share in Allianz for six shares in Hypo-Bank would run from August 4 to September 10.

Among other shares, Lufthansa AG was up seven pfennigs at 37.02 marks in post-bourse IBIS after the Bonn government said it would sell off its remaining stake in the airline this fall, which it said was worth five billion marks.
